question.prompt: Paula the painter and her two helpers each paint at constant, but different, rates. They always start at \(8{:}00\) AM and all three always take the same amount of time to eat lunch. On Monday the three of them painted \(50\%\) of a house, quitting at \(4{:}00\) PM. On Tuesday, when Paula wasn’t there, the two helpers painted only \(24\%\) of the house and quit at \(2{:}12\) PM. On Wednesday Paula worked by herself and finished the house by working until \(7{:}12\) PM. How long, in minutes, was each day’s lunch break?

solutions.explanation:
Treat the two helpers as one team, whose constant rate is the sum of their individual rates. Wednesday's remaining work was
\[
100\%-50\%-24\%=26\%.
\]
Thus Tuesday and Wednesday together produced \(50\%\) of the house, exactly the amount painted on Monday.

The elapsed times from 8:00 AM were \(480\), \(372\), and \(672\) minutes on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Since every lunch has the same length, the helpers worked \(480-372=108\) fewer minutes on Tuesday than on Monday, while Paula worked \(672-480=192\) more minutes on Wednesday than on Monday.

Because the later days' total output equals Monday's output, Paula's extra \(192\) minutes must replace the work the helpers would have done in their missing \(108\) minutes. Their rates therefore satisfy
\[
\text{Paula's rate}:\text{helpers' combined rate}
=108:192=9:16.
\]
On Monday they worked for equal amounts of time, so their contributions had this same ratio. The helpers painted
\[
50\%\cdot\frac{16}{9+16}=32\%
\]
of the house that day.

At their constant rate, painting \(24\%\) on Tuesday took \(24/32=3/4\) of their Monday working time. The difference of \(108\) minutes is consequently one quarter of Monday's working time. Monday contained \(4\cdot108=432\) working minutes, leaving
\[
480-432=48
\]
minutes for lunch. The answer is \(\boxed{48}\) minutes, choice D.
solutions.title: Compare extra and missing working time
